historical_reviews.deepseek: Does not analyze expander register semantics or instance routing.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Identifies multiplicity ambiguity but provides no per-instance selection or pin-level expected-state oracle.
historical_reviews.related_cases: Row137 had two switch instances at one address. Here registers0x00 and0x01 plausibly represent separate port banks within one0x74 expander, so they must not be counted as the three named devices without PID proof.

original_test_intent: Verify BMC I2C-10 reaches the IO expander on HMC and the separate IO expanders on both carrier boards, with correct read-only port state for every named instance and no GPIO changes.
original_method: Map BMC I2C-10 to bus9 and enumerate the three expander instances/selection paths from PID1114953; identify address and part per instance; inspect driver ownership and direction/output state; read only the approved input/status registers (including0x00/0x01 where applicable); compare pin masks against platform presence/strap state; repeat independently for HMC, carrier A and carrier B; verify directions/outputs remain unchanged.
manual_activity: BMC/HMC/carrier owner supplies three-instance topology, part/register/pin maps, expected masks and driver-safe access/recovery; physical probing is not inferred.
required_inputs: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-10 to bus9 and HMC/carrier-A/carrier-B expander instances
Per-instance upstream mux/segment selection and address, especially any repeated0x74 alias
Expander part/revision and definitions for registers0x00/0x01, including input/output/config semantics
Expected pin name, polarity, direction and input/status mask for each instance
Kernel/daemon GPIO expander bindings and owner-approved driver interface or force exception
Timeout/NACK/error criteria, unchanged output/direction verification and recovery
safety_requirements: Do not equate two register offsets with two or three devices
Do not run broad quick-write discovery on bus9
Prefer GPIO/driver read interfaces and avoid `-f` on a bound expander unless explicitly approved
Confirm0x00/0x01 are read-safe for the exact part; never write direction/output registers
Capture and compare direction/output state; abort on any GPIO transition, device ambiguity, NACK, timeout, stuck bus or management regression
agent_execution_scope: Collect three expander identities/routes, driver bindings and GPIO direction/output/input baselines
After approval, select and read each expander separately and compare pin masks
Do not probe/solder, scan blindly, infer instances from register count, force bound devices by default, change GPIO, auto-retry or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve register semantics and pin/polarity/direction/value oracle for each
Approve driver-safe access or exceptional `-f`, timeout and recovery
Review separate HMC/carrier-A/carrier-B evidence and issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Incorrect physical-only substitution; source supplies functional expander reads.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Do not use broad `i2cdetect -q`. After instance/driver approval, use `i2ctransfer -f -y 9 w1@0x74 0x01 r1` and `... 0x00 r1` only for the instance whose part defines those input registers; repeat through authoritative selection/address paths for the other expanders and verify GPIO state remains unchanged.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC bus9, address0x74, registers0x01/0x00, r1, BMC I2C-10, HMC plus both carrier expanders, PID1114953 and 15/5-minute scope are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Capture a read-only device/register/pin matrix for each of the three expanders through its proven route and compare expected input masks without altering outputs.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds three-instance identity and pin-level acceptance, distinguishes ports from devices, and removes invented physical probing and unsafe broad scan dependence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Registers0x00 and0x01 can be two port banks of a single expander; even correct bytes from one0x74 cannot prove the two other physical expander instances.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Forced access can race GPIO consumers; wrong part/register assumptions may touch outputs or clear latched inputs; static values validate current state but not every GPIO transition path.

project_override_considerations: Wistron I2C policy requires controller/bus, every target instance/address and expected response. GPIO expander ownership and output preservation are mandatory because these pins may control platform hardware.
expected_evidence: PID topology for BMC I2C-10/bus9 to HMC, carrier-A and carrier-B expanders
Register and pin/polarity/direction/value oracle for each expander
Timestamped read transcript and expected-versus-observed masks per instance
Pre/post configuration/output/input state showing no unintended GPIO change
BMC/bus/consumer health and engineer verdict for all three instances

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source names three expanders but provides two offsets at one address with no routing or pin oracle; those offsets may belong to one device. It also omits driver ownership and earlier reviews invent physical probing.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The multi-instance connectivity goal is clear; platform maps and register/pin contracts are standard owner inputs, so this is RPUC.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row140 Wistron-HW Robust-00018-V002: provide PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-10/bus9 to the HMC, carrier-A and carrier-B IO expander instances, including selector/address/part per device. Define whether0x74 registers0x00/0x01 are input ports, expected pin/polarity/direction/value masks for each instance, driver ownership and whether `-f` is allowed, safe scan policy, no-GPIO-change verification, timeouts and recovery. Confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.

review_improvement: Restores remote functional coverage and exposes the source's central device-count versus register-count ambiguity, adding per-instance pin/state preservation evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Two register reads do not imply two devices: many multi-port expanders expose adjacent input registers. Because the title requires three physical instances, the agent must traverse a documented selector/address path for each and compare pin-level state. The dominant safety risk is not lack of photos but bypassing a GPIO driver or misreading a register map, which could affect platform control pins. Read-only driver-aware evidence is sufficient once mapped.
